name: Foundation of Tenochtitlan
summary: The Mexica (Aztec) people found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, guided (according to tradition) by the omen of an eagle devouring a snake. The island location provides defensive advantages; chinampas (floating gardens) enable intensive agriculture. By 1500, Tenochtitlan has a population of 200,000–300,000, making it one of the world's largest cities.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Aztec Empire becomes the dominant power in Mesoamerica by 1500, controlling a tributary system of millions; its destruction by Cortés in 1521 represents one of the most consequential colonial encounters in history.
